content:
Earlier in July, Apple updated its TestFlight app, adding basic search functionality. You might think this simple update would receive unanimous praise, but the same TestFlight app has introduced a rather annoying bug for many users.

Personally, I wasn't noticeably affected by this bug. So at the time I felt the TestFlight update was a simple but important improvement.

Sometimes a small change can have a big impact. This is especially true for users with a large library of pre-loaded software when it comes to Apple's latest TestFlight update. Apple has just updated TestFlight across iPhone, iPad, Mac, and other platforms. The new version 4.3 introduces a 'search bar for quickly finding apps'.

In hindsight, I did notice something strange, which I flagged at the end of the post (though my judgment at the time was the other way round):

The reason I missed this bug is that two years ago I merged my previously separate iCloud and App Store Apple accounts, leaving behind several years of TestFlight app records. Although the process wasn't exactly convenient, it was worth it for me.

In any case, I'm not the only one who noticed the TestFlight app bug. John Vorhees from MacStories also mentioned it:

So you can imagine how excited I was when I saw Zac Hall's article on 9to5Mac about TestFlight getting a search bar. I thought to myself: 'Finally!' I immediately stopped what I was doing and updated the app. [...] Unfortunately, there's a big 'but' to this story. Previously, TestFlight betas were arranged in reverse chronological order, which I quite liked. [...] As a result, these expired betas are now scattered among the currently active TestFlight betas in alphabetical order, and the list of expired betas seems to have expanded to include every beta I've ever participated in. I did a rough count and for me, there are nearly 800 app records. As you can imagine, very few of the betas on this list are actually active. The search helps a little, but it's no longer possible to find things by scrolling.

Later in August, John Gruber wrote an article on Daring Fireball about the TestFlight update and the bug:

Last night, more than a month after this bug appeared (and was flagged by Vorhees), Apple finally updated TestFlight for the first time. Although the update notes only mention bug fixes, this update has indeed fixed the relevant bug.

Version 4.3.1 of TestFlight is the fix provided for users affected by this regression.
